content.title: Key Takeaways
items: A single prompt is not a content system. A workflow connects research, a brief, context, prompting, drafting, fact-checking, editorial review, and integrity checking into one repeatable sequence.
Prompt quality depends on more than wording. It depends on the context, evidence, constraints, and verification steps built around the prompt.
AI should draft, structure, and organize approved information. AI should not invent facts, sources, statistics, testimonials, or professional conclusions.

Breaking one big request into a chain of smaller, single-purpose prompts (research, brief, draft, fact-check, integrity check, final QA) produces more reliable, more reviewable output than asking AI to 'do it all' in one pass.
A Content Integrity Audit — comparing the AI draft against the approved source material — is one of the most important and most frequently skipped steps in AI content production.
The goal is not to accumulate hundreds of prompts. The goal is a small number of tested, versioned, reusable prompts that plug into a repeatable operating system.

content.title: 1. What Is an AI Prompt Workflow?

items.definition: A repeatable sequence that determines what AI receives, what AI is asked to do, what AI produces, how that output is reviewed, and what happens after it is approved — connecting research, briefs, prompt chaining, fact auditing, and integrity checks into one system.

content.content: An AI prompt workflow treats the prompt as one instruction inside a larger, connected chain of steps. The prompt is the instruction; the workflow is everything that has to happen before and after that instruction for it to produce something trustworthy.

content.content: Define what the content must achieve: educate readers, answer a recurring FAQ, explain a process step-by-step, assist decision support, provide an actionable checklist, or support local discovery.
Specify business type, role (patient, client, buyer, tenant), experience level, problem, search intent, location, and decision stage. Audience specificity is high-leverage input.
Assemble verified research notes, primary sources, business facts, customer questions, review themes, and approved internal knowledge. Connects to Article #21.
Translate research into a structured brief before writing drafting prompts. Connects to Article #22.
Assemble relevant context: business info, audience definition, topic, research, sources, brand voice, content brief, compliance constraints, and output format. Relevant context > maximum context.
Convert brief and context into an operational prompt defining role, task, context, inputs, requirements, exclusions, format, quality standards, and verification.
Break complex content generation into a staged sequence: Research → Outline → Draft → Fact Check → Improve → SEO/GEO Review → Final QA.
Define explicit contracts for each prompt stage: INPUT (received), PROCESS (action taken), OUTPUT (returned), and QUALITY (evaluation standard).

content.title: 14. Eight Reusable Prompts for the Workflow
Prompt 1: Research Organizer
content.prompt:
Role: Research organizer for [BUSINESS NAME], a [BUSINESS TYPE] serving [LOCATION].
Input: The following research materials — [PASTE RESEARCH / NOTES].
Task: Organize this research into a table (Key fact, Source, Date, Relevance to [TOPIC], Confidence, Missing info).
Constraints: Do not invent facts not present in supplied research. Flag outdated items.

content.title: Prompt 2: Content Brief Builder
content.prompt:
Role: Content brief builder for [BUSINESS NAME].
Input: Organized research table, Content goal: [GOAL], Audience: [AUDIENCE], Topic: [TOPIC].
Task: Build a content brief (Objective, Audience, Primary/Secondary questions, Key points with sources, FAQs, Risks).
Constraints: Every key point must trace to supplied research. Mark unsourced points 'Needs Source'.

content.title: Prompt 3: Content Drafting
content.prompt:
Role: Content drafter for [BUSINESS NAME], writing in [BRAND VOICE].
Input: Approved content brief and verified research.
Task: Write a full Markdown draft following the brief's structure.
Rules: Preserve all qualifications. Do not invent facts, statistics, sources, or testimonials.

content.title: Prompt 4: Fact and Source Auditor
content.prompt:
Role: Fact and source auditor.
Input: Draft + verified research.
Task: Audit every claim, statistic, date, and URL against supplied research. Output table (Claim, Status: PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL, Source, Notes).
Constraints: Unmatched claims must be marked FAIL, not assumed correct.

content.title: Prompt 5: Content Quality Editor
content.prompt:
Role: Content quality editor.
Input: Fact-checked draft.
Task: Evaluate (do not rewrite) clarity, audience usefulness, structure, specificity, redundancy, and tone. Output issue list with recommendations.

content.title: Prompt 6: SEO / GEO Content Auditor
content.prompt:
Role: SEO/GEO content auditor.
Input: Edited draft.
Task: Evaluate intent alignment, topical coverage, heading structure, internal links, entity clarity, and explicit definitions.
Constraints: Do not recommend keyword stuffing or claim ranking guarantees.

content.title: Prompt 7: Content Integrity Auditor
content.prompt:
Role: Content integrity auditor.
Input: Approved source brief + current AI draft.
Task: Compare line-by-line for omitted sections, merged paragraphs, missing examples/FAQs/tables, altered meaning, or removed qualifications.
Output: PASS / PARTIAL / FAIL report. The draft must never reduce approved meaning.

content.title: Prompt 8: Final Publishing QA
content.prompt:
Role: Final publishing QA reviewer.
Input: Fully edited, fact-checked, integrity-checked draft.
Task: Verify title, headings, lists, tables, links, FAQ section, source citations, and disclaimers. Output publish-readiness checklist.

content.title: 15. The Complete AI Prompt Master Workflow

nodes.label: Fact Check, Quality Edit & SEO/GEO Audit

content.content: Organize prompts into functional categories: Research, Brief, Writing, Editing, Fact Checking, SEO, GEO, FAQ, Checklist, Workflow, Repurposing, Update, Audit, and Integrity.
Track Prompt ID, Name, Version, Purpose, Input, Output, Owner, Last Tested, and Status (Draft, Tested, Approved, Deprecated).
Test prompts against normal, incomplete, ambiguous, high-risk, long, and contradictory inputs to evaluate factuality, consistency, completeness, format compliance, and hallucination risk.
Common failure modes: vague instructions, irrelevant context, missing source material, conflicting rules, unconstrained claims, verbosity, and generic output.

content.title: 10 Common Prompt Workflow Mistakes
content.content:
1. Treating prompts as magic content creators without human review
2. Using vague instructions without contextual grounding
3. Providing no source material and expecting factual accuracy
4. Asking one prompt to perform research, drafting, and editing simultaneously
5. Skipping mandatory fact-checking and human editorial review
6. Allowing AI to invent statistics, sources, or testimonials
7. Copying competitor structures directly
8. Trimming drafts for length by removing necessary qualifications or disclaimers
9. Untested prompts published directly to production
10. Skipping the Content Integrity Audit

content.title: 32. What AI Can and Cannot Do

pros: Structure information and transform research into drafts
Classify, organize, and audit content against criteria
Identify gaps against a brief and adapt formats
Improve clarity, tone consistency, and readability
cons: Cannot guarantee factual accuracy or current information
Cannot guarantee professional correctness (medical, legal, financial)
Cannot guarantee search rankings or AI visibility
Cannot replace human verification of primary regulatory/clinical sources

items.question: What is an AI prompt workflow?
items.answer: An AI prompt workflow is a repeatable sequence — research, brief, context, prompt, draft, fact-check, review, and publish — determining what AI receives, what it does, and how output is verified before publication.

items.question: What is the difference between a prompt and a workflow?
items.answer: A prompt is a single instruction given to AI. A workflow is a connected sequence of steps (research, brief, draft, fact-check, review) moving from goal to verified publication.

items.question: How can businesses reduce AI hallucinations?
items.answer: Supply verified source material, instruct AI explicitly not to invent facts, and execute a dedicated fact-and-source audit comparing draft claims against supplied research.

items.question: What is prompt chaining?
items.answer: Prompt chaining connects single-purpose prompts sequentially, where the output of one stage (e.g. Research Organizer) becomes the input for the next (e.g. Brief Builder).
